findings.title: design.md §9's own re-anchor paragraph contradicts §0 and records a git diff output that does not reproduce: it asserts no code citation moved when the second hop moved a code file the plan edits
findings.where: design.md §9, opening paragraph and the command block immediately under it (around :2261-2272)
findings.problem: §9 states: '**1 ahead / 12 behind**. The single intervening commit is **docs-and-outputs only**, so no code citation moved' and records 'git diff e9e377ce..origin/stack --stat -> 12 files, +2121/-1, no amplify/ scripts/ src/ tests/'. Neither is true at 061b6e77. There are TWO intervening commits (4fe31824, then 061b6e77) and the actual range diff is 16 files, +3905/-14, and it DOES contain amplify/functions/messaging/whatsapp-business-api/handler.py and tests/test_audit_payment_diagnostic.py. The recorded figures are the e9e377ce..4fe31824 hop-1 diff pasted against the full range. §0 of the same document gets this exactly right - it documents both hops, states 'Hop 2 DID touch code', and re-derives the +12/+13 shift for nine citations in that handler. So the two sections disagree on the single most load-bearing fact in the plan: whether the whatsapp-business-api citations moved. Those citations are load-bearing for F-9's native reach-path (:5996-6000), F-4's live sites and F-6, all scheduled under §5 row 4b-ii. A coder or owner who reads §9 - the section the author offers as proof of resolution - concludes no re-derivation is needed in that file and ships against stale line numbers, which is precisely the failure §0 exists to prevent and which round 3 finding 4 already punished once.
findings.fix:
Replace the §9 paragraph and block with §0's actual facts, and make §9 point at §0 rather than restate it:

'**Base re-anchored first, before any finding was touched.** The review verified against `e9e377ce`; `origin/stack` is now `061b6e77` - **1 ahead / 12 behind**. The base moved **twice** during this resolution pass and **hop 2 changed code**. See §0 for the per-citation re-derivation; the summary is: hop 1 (`e9e377ce`->`4fe31824`) was docs-and-outputs only; hop 2 (`4fe31824`->`061b6e77`) edited `amplify/functions/messaging/whatsapp-business-api/handler.py` and `tests/test_audit_payment_diagnostic.py`, shifting every citation in that handler below line 321 by **+12** and below 6106 by **+13**. Two document citations in the QA-send authority chain also moved.'

```
git diff e9e377ce..4fe31824 --stat      -> 12 files, +2121/-1,  docs/outputs only
git diff 4fe31824..origin/stack --stat  -> 11 files, +1784/-13, INCLUDES CODE
git diff e9e377ce..origin/stack --stat  -> 16 files, +3905/-14, INCLUDES CODE
```

findings.title: §9's verification-coverage claim contradicts itself in consecutive sentences: 139 citations re-verified, 97 pass
findings.problem: '**139 load-bearing citations were individually re-verified** at `061b6e77` ... All 97 pass.' A reader cannot tell whether the re-derivation covered 97 or 139 citations, nor what became of the 42-citation difference - and 'All 97 pass' reads as a complete pass over a set whose size is contradicted one line earlier. This is the headline assurance the whole §9 table rests on, in a document whose central lesson is that an unverified number is not evidence. Spot-checking found no actually-failing citation among the ones I reproduced, so this is a bookkeeping conflict rather than a hidden failure - but as written the claim cannot be audited.
findings.fix: State one number and keep the two concepts separate, e.g.: '**139 load-bearing citations were individually re-verified** at `061b6e77` with `git grep -n` plus a per-line `git show | sed -n '<n>p'` substring assertion. **All 139 reproduce; 11 carried changed values, each listed in the row that uses it.**' If 97 was the count actually re-checked by hand and 139 the total inventory, say exactly that: '139 load-bearing citations exist; **97 were re-verified individually** this pass (the remainder are unchanged document citations in files neither hop touched, named here: ...).'
